1.original: J'yhuh Tia's final lesson for you is the strongest technique of Kornago beastmasters. It demands an understanding of the universality of life, and the ability to harness the shift of all that is inevitable. With no little pressure upon your shoulders, you approach the striking dummy.

2.original: It takes time and no little hard work, but finally you bring to bear the wisdom of the Kornago. Looking round to J'yhuh Tia, you have never seen a teacher quite so proud.

3.original: Despite your significant strength, your Cu Sith whines its unease. Hardly surprising, Lauda supplies, given the fate of its previous master. Again, she has arrived, this time her hair dark and gaze steady. She shares the story of her encounter with the Cu Sith's former guardian, Philkin. Upon learning of her plight, Philkin offered to transfer Guttler's soul into the depths of the Crucible, removing most of his control over Lauda's physical body. His generosity proved his undoing, however, for Guttler awoke as he worked. In a race against time, Philkin finished the transfer just before Lauda struck him down with Guttler's axe. The dying beastmaster spent his final breath urging his Cu Sith to flee.

4.original: With Philkin's fate heavy in your heart, you set off for Bentbranch Meadows. It is time to put an end to the misery that vengeance has wrought.

5.original: Lauda warns you that Guttler may assume her form upon the third board, but says to spare him no mercy as he will offer none in return. While she will be helpless to assist you in battle, she is prepared to face Guttler upon his defeat and prays you emerge triumphant for the sake of all trapped in this endless curse of bloodshed.<hex:02100103><hex:02100103>※The next beastmaster quest will be available from Lauda upon clearing the Third Board of the Unbroken.

24.original: Complete an infinitive combo on the dummy.

48.original: ...Heh. Look how far you've come. You do me proud, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>.

49.original: The final lesson I can offer is the deepest wisdom of our ancestors.

50.original: When we stride beneath the sun, we carry the moon in our hearts. When we stalk the moon, the sun within burns ever bright. By marrying our opposites, man and beast may come to understand the totality of nature. A universality, if you will.

60.original: That's my star pupil. Now all that's left is to put those teachings into practice.

61.original: Haha, take as much time as you need. While an abstract concept, it may be better understood through practice.

62.original: ...Then we're two of a kind, because I felt just as clueless once. Meditate upon what you've learned thus far, and you'll discover the answer soon enough.

63.original: Hold universality in your heart and focus it upon a striking dummy. Lead the sun to the moon, and the moon to the sun. Bring to bear the fundamental truth of existence.

64.original: By chaining the opposing instinctual affinities <hex:024804F201FA03><hex:024904F201FB03>Sunstrider<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> and <hex:024804F201FA03><hex:024904F201FB03>Moonstalker<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>, you will complete the infinitive combo <hex:024804F201FA03><hex:024904F201FB03>Universality<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>.

65.original: Learn more about infinitive combos via the <hex:021202B703> icon in the <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>duty list<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>.

73.original: Combining opposites creates a strength without equal. Like the turning of day to night, and night to day─harnessing inevitability is the key.

74.original: By chaining the opposing instinctual affinities <hex:024804F201FA03><hex:024904F201FB03>Sunstrider<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> and <hex:024804F201FA03><hex:024904F201FB03>Moonstalker<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>, you will complete the infinitive combo <hex:024804F201FA03><hex:024904F201FB03>Universality<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>.

75.original: Learn more about infinitive combos via the <hex:021202B703> icon in the <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>duty list<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103>.

83.original: Phenomenal. You're a true Kornago beastmaster, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. Let us take a moment to reflect.

84.original: Your partner has grown strong, little one.

86.original: ...But it has known a strong guardian before. It worries for your safety.

88.original: (-Lauda-)'Tis little wonder. It watched its former master die.

89.original: ...I debated when to reveal this, but you deserve to know.

90.original: Our client should be nearby. Won't it be nice to meet a kindred soul?

93.original: Pardon me! Are you the one in search of beastmasters?

95.original: Come any closer, and I might... I may kill you.

96.original: Then let us speak at this distance. My name is Philkin. Who are you?

97.original: A beastmaster. Of the Lhu. The axe before me has sealed within it the soul of a forest guardian. He possesses my body, and I...I cannot escape him...

98.original: ...By the sound of it, I believe transferring Guttler's soul from the axe to those training grounds you described may offer recourse.

99.original: That way, his presence will be confined within the Crucible. At the very least, his hold upon your physical body will become extremely difficult to maintain.

100.original: Such a mighty soul would be difficult to disperse, but I should be capable of sealing it.

101.original: 'Twould be generosity I could not begin to repay...

102.original: Helping a fellow beastmaster hardly warrants payment. Though, I'll not refuse a pint if offered.

104.original: Come out to play, has he? I knew he would be strong, but this...

106.original: Either I fetter you, or you slay me. Let's make this quick.

107.original: Beastmaster... Plague upon the wilds... Thy soul is forfeit!

111.original: So Philkin sealed Guttler as deep within the Crucible as he could. To ease his hold upon you.

114.original: You are not alone. You never will be.

117.original: ...As is mine. I will not shy from what awaits.

119.original: But I won't hasten you. We await your arrival at Bentbranch Meadows.

120.original: I believe in you, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. And so do your familiars.

122.original: <hex:02080CE905FF04536865FF03486503> has come to challenge the third board, and to defeat Guttler.

123.original: And so <hex:02080CE905FF04736865FF03686503> shall. However, be advised that Guttler may assume my likeness during battle.

124.original: Control over me yields him great satisfaction. Making clear who the master is between us.

125.original: He means to compound our suffering with illusions, but you must not grant any quarter to the shade he fashions. Guttler is within, and he will offer no mercy.

127.original: ...but I will pray for your victory. And I will face him.

128.original: As a member of the Lhu, I will accept Guttler's anger and grief. I will flee from the truth no longer.

129.original: ...That is my path as a beastmaster.

134.original: Knock some sense into him, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. Off you go.

135.original: Then allow me to open the third board.

136.original: The Third Board of the Unbroken has been unlocked. To challenge it, speak with Lauda in Bentbranch Meadows.

137.original: Furthermore, new wares are now available from the Kornago merchant.
